newsitem.title: USA: Continental, pilots to start talking money.
newsitem.headline: Continental, pilots to start talking money.

text.p: Contract talks between Continental Airlines Inc and its pilots' union are likely to shift this week to the critical issues of pay and benefits after weeks of negotiations on less substantive matters, a union spokesman said on Monday.

The pilots, who have been flying with green "Show me the money" luggage tags to press their wage demands, are seeking up to 38 percent pay hikes in the wake of record profits posted by the Houston-based airline in recent quarters.

Independent Association of Continental Pilots spokesman Jim Moody told Reuters the company was expected in talks here on Tuesday to make a counteroffer to the union's proposal for a contract to replace the current one, which expires June 30.
If that occurred, he said, "they would be opening negotiations in compensation, retirement and all those areas that are the major portions (of the contract)," Moody said.
Negotiators representing the airline and its 5,000-member pilots union traded draft proposals to open the talks on April 2.
The company has said it hopes to have a new contract hammered out by July 1, but pilots say the deadline is less important than getting a good pact.
"We'd love to have a great contract by July 1, but it's not going to tie our hands," Moody said.
He said tentative agreements already have been reached on a number of sidebar issues such as seniority, training, physical examinations, union security and a new section on alcohol and drug testing.

Continental, the nation's fifth-largest carrier, in April reported its eighth straight quarter of record profits with $124 million in pre-tax income and ended the period with $927 million in cash on hand.
